executionSummary: Re-execution confirmed SAP Fiori shell bar lazy-loads action buttons. After login, 'Open Search' button appears automatically within 2-3 seconds. No prerequisite action needed. Previous patch (TC-CS-021) used incorrect workaround.

failingStepResult.action: Click the search icon in the shell bar

triedLocators.note: Shell bar rendered only basic elements: Open Menu, SAP Logo, Home, Profile
After 3-second wait, button appeared in DOM automatically — full shell bar rendered with: Open Search, Joule, Open Help, Notifications, Profile
Button clicked successfully, search bar opened

timingRequirement.description: Wait for shell bar to complete JavaScript initialization
timingRequirement.waitStrategy: Wait for button.isVisible() with timeout, NOT fixed delay

failingStepResult.resolutionNote: SAP Fiori shell bar uses progressive rendering. Action buttons (Open Search, Joule, Open Help, Notifications) are added to the DOM asynchronously after initial page load. No user interaction required — buttons appear automatically once JavaScript initialization completes.

previousPatchAnalysis.approach: Click 'Open Menu' button to trigger shell bar full render
previousPatchAnalysis.issue: During manual MCP re-execution for TC-CS-021, the delay between actions gave shell bar time to render naturally. The 'Open Menu' click was coincidental timing, not causal. Automated script runs faster, exposing the flaw.
previousPatchAnalysis.correctSolution: Simple wait for button visibility — no prerequisite action

sapBehaviorNotes: SAP Fiori is functioning correctly. The shell bar lazy-loading is an intentional performance optimization, not a defect.
patchStrategy: Remove flawed 'Open Menu' prerequisite logic. Replace with simple wait: `await searchBtn.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 30000 })`. Locator is correct — only timing/wait strategy needs fixing.

evidenceCapture.t0_afterLogin: Shell bar showed: Open Menu, SAP Logo, Home, Profile. No 'Open Search' button.
evidenceCapture.t3_afterWait: Shell bar showed: Open Menu, SAP Logo, Home, Open Search, Joule, Open Help, Notifications, Profile. Full render complete.
evidenceCapture.searchOpened: Search bar appeared with searchbox ref=e473 active.

sapUIBehaviorNotes: SAP Fiori Launchpad splits shell bar rendering into two phases: (1) Essential navigation (Home, Profile, Menu) renders immediately; (2) Action buttons (Search, Joule, Help, Notifications) render asynchronously 2-3 seconds later after JavaScript modules load. This is standard lazy-loading for performance optimization. Scripts must account for this delay by waiting for button visibility rather than assuming immediate availability.
